entry.title: Mac-style Text Navigation 0.1
entry.content:
Mac-style Text Navigation

Makes the modifier keys behave like on macOS when moving the text cursor: Ctrl acts like Cmd and Alt acts like Option.

Shortcut Does the same as (Windows) macOS equivalent
Ctrl + ← Home (start of line) Cmd + ←
Ctrl + → End (end of line) Cmd + →
Alt + ← Ctrl + ← (previous word) Option + ←
Alt + → Ctrl + → (next word) Option + →

Holding Shift as well extends the selection, as expected.

Notes

  • The mod runs in a dedicated background windhawk.exe process and uses a global low-level keyboard hook, so it works in every application.
  • The remapping applies everywhere, not only in text fields. For example, Alt+Left/Right no longer go Back/Forward in browsers, File Explorer and Settings, and Ctrl+Left/Right lose app-specific meanings (such as jumping to the edge of a data region in Excel). Use the "Excluded programs" setting for apps where you want the original behavior.
  • Windows running as administrator are not affected unless Windhawk itself runs elevated (a Windows security restriction).
  • Ctrl+Alt combinations (including AltGr) and combinations with the Win key are left untouched.
  • Modifiers produced by remapping tools that inject input (e.g. PowerToys Keyboard Manager, AutoHotkey) are not recognized. Remaps done through the scancode map (e.g. SharpKeys) work.

entry.title: Ookla Speed Test for Network Menu 1.0
entry.content:
Ookla Speed Test for Network Menu

Right-clicking the network icon in the Windows 11 taskbar and choosing Run internet speed test normally opens a web page in your browser. This mod replaces it with a native flyout above the taskbar that runs the official Ookla Speedtest CLI in the background and shows the test live.

Screenshots

Download Upload History

Features

  • Live gauge (0 to 2,000+ Mbps) drawn as a soft light bar with smooth motion: blue for download, purple for upload.
  • Ping, jitter, download and upload measured by Ookla. The server is always picked automatically.
  • Test history: when a test finishes, the flyout moves to a list of the last 100 tests (date and time, IP, server, download, upload, ping) with the new test on top. Click a row to open its result page on speedtest.net.
  • Copy puts the result, including the speedtest.net link, on the clipboard.
  • Follows the Windows light/dark theme, transparency, DPI and the "Animation effects" setting. Keyboard (Tab, arrows, Enter, Esc) and screen reader accessible.
  • Interface in English or Portuguese, following the Windows display language.

Requirements

  1. Download the Speedtest CLI for Windows from speedtest.net/apps/cli and extract speedtest.exe.
  2. Put it at %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\speedtest\speedtest.exe (the default), or set its path in the mod settings.

Ookla license and privacy

Before the first test, the flyout explains what Ookla receives and links Ookla's EULA, Terms of Use and Privacy Policy. No test runs until you click Accept and test. Only then does the mod start speedtest.exe with --accept-license --accept-gdpr. The acceptance is stored separately for each Windows user.

The Speedtest CLI also records the acceptance in its own file, %APPDATA%\Ookla\Speedtest CLI\speedtest-cli.ini, which stays after the mod is removed. Delete that folder to reset it.

Network access

The mod opens no connections itself. It runs speedtest.exe, which:

  • contacts Ookla's servers to pick a test server, then downloads from and uploads to that Speedtest server;
  • uploads the result to speedtest.net, where Ookla stores it (the result link in the history points there).

Ookla receives your public IP address, your internet provider and the test results, under its privacy policy.

A test runs every time the flyout opens, and on Start, Repeat or Retry. Set Start the test automatically to Never to make tests click-only (Auto already waits for a click on metered connections). Clicking a history row or a terms link opens speedtest.net in your browser.

Data usage

Ookla does not cap a test: on a 2 Gbps line one test moves about 4-5 GB. With Start the test automatically set to Auto, the flyout waits for a click when Windows reports the connection as metered.

Notes

  • Stop, Esc, closing the flyout or disabling the mod ends speedtest.exe immediately (it runs inside a kill-on-close job object).
  • The history lives in the mod's own Windhawk storage, separately for each Windows user, and is removed with the mod.
  • Network Menu Speed Test intercepts the same link. If both are installed, disable one of them.

Credits

Based on Network Menu Speed Test by Alessandro-Vecchio, which provides the hooks and the original flyout. This mod swaps its Cloudflare engine for the Ookla Speedtest CLI and adds the light bar, the smooth motion and the test history.

entry.title: Volu - macOS Volume HUD 1.0.0
entry.content:
Volu - macOS Volume HUD

Authentic macOS-style translucent volume HUD for Windows with classic step click sounds.

Features

  • Pixel-perfect design: Authentic macOS frosted glass HUD overlay with clean 16-step volume bar and soft drop shadow.
  • Audio feedback: Classic wooden and modern tactile volume step clicks. Silent on mute.
  • Smooth animations: Smooth fade-out transition with configurable on-screen duration.
  • Flexible positioning: Place the HUD at the center, top, or bottom of your screen.
  • Optional hotkeys: Global shortcuts (Ctrl + Alt + Up, Ctrl + Alt + Down, Ctrl + Alt + V), disabled by default to avoid shortcut conflicts.
  • Native flyout suppression: Intercepts physical media keys (Volume Up, Volume Down, Mute) system-wide using RegisterHotKey, suppressing the default Windows flyouts.
  • 1/16 Quantization: Each key press changes volume by 1/16 (6.25%) matching macOS, instead of Windows' default 2%.
  • Dynamic device switching: Automatically follows the default audio output device when headphones, speakers, or Bluetooth devices are connected.

Key Capture & Shortcuts

The mod captures physical volume keys system-wide via RegisterHotKey, so other apps no longer receive the volume keys:

  • Volume Up — Increase volume by 6.25% (1 step)
  • Volume Down — Decrease volume by 6.25% (1 step)
  • Volume Mute — Toggle mute

Optional shortcuts (if enabled in settings):

  • Ctrl + Alt + Up — Volume Up
  • Ctrl + Alt + Down — Volume Down
  • Ctrl + Alt + V — Mute / Unmute

Comparison with Other OSD Mods

Unlike win10-volume-brightness-osd (which restores Windows 8/10 flyouts with brightness controls) or osd-custom-pill (which provides modern animated pills), Volu is focused exclusively on authentic macOS volume HUD fidelity:

  • Classic square frosted glass aesthetics with multi-pass soft drop shadow.
  • Authentic wooden and tactile step clicks.
  • 16-step quantization (6.25% per step) strictly synchronizing with the 16-segment bar.
  • Lightweight tool mod architecture dedicated solely to volume control.

entry.title: Sharp Taskbar Icons After Remote Desktop 1.0
entry.content:
Sharp Taskbar Icons After Remote Desktop

Connecting with Remote Desktop from a device with a different display scale (for example the Microsoft Remote Desktop app on a phone, at 200–300%) switches the session to that scale, and Explorer renders the tray icons for it. When you come back to the local screen, Explorer doesn't render them again from the programs' icons — it rescales the copies it already made, so they stay blurry until the program or Explorer is restarted.

This mod asks Explorer to render the icons again. For the tray it uses the copy of each icon that Explorer itself keeps for the tray button; as a fallback (for icons it can't find there), it remembers the icon each program gives the tray, by watching the WM_COPYDATA messages that Shell_NotifyIcon sends to the taskbar and Explorer's answers to them. When the session returns to the local console, it waits until the scale has stayed the same for a few seconds (Explorer may pass through an intermediate scale, and turns tray requests down while it rebuilds the taskbar) and then:

  • asks Explorer to render every tray icon again (NIM_MODIFY with the icon Explorer itself keeps for that tray button, or the program's own icon handle for icons that aren't in the tray toolbars — what happens when the program is restarted, but without restarting anything). Explorer's copy is used because many programs destroy the handle they give the tray right after giving it;
  • asks the taskbar to re-read the icon of every top-level window (HSHELL_REDRAW through the taskbar's shell hook message). Buttons of pinned programs that aren't running are not refreshed.

If Explorer turns most tray icons down because it is still busy, or the scale changes again, the tray is refreshed again (for about a minute after returning).

While the remote session is active, the mod checks the taskbar's scale every few seconds. If it never differed from the local screen's scale, nothing is done. The Windhawk log shows the scales and how many icons were refreshed.

Icons that existed before the mod was enabled are handled too: their copies are read from the tray at refresh time. The exception is an icon a program registered by GUID before the mod was loaded: Explorer only accepts it by its GUID, which the mod learns when the program registers or updates the icon. Nothing is sent to other programs.

Made for the Windows 10 taskbar (tested on Windows 10 22H2), and for Windows 11 versions whose taskbar still behaves like it; not tested on the newer Windows 11 taskbar. The newer Windows 11 (XAML) notification area has no tray toolbars, so there only icons registered while the mod was running are refreshed.

entry.title: ZoneShift - Per-App Timezone Spoofer 1.0.0
entry.content:
ZoneShift - Per-App Timezone Spoofer

ZoneShift is a lightweight, high-performance Windhawk mod that spoofs the time zone and local time for individual Windows applications without changing the system clock or affecting other running programs.

Why Per-App Timezone Spoofing?

  1. Wallpaper Engine & Desktop Customization:

    • Web wallpapers (Chromium/CEF), Scene wallpapers (DirectX/native), and Edge wallpapers can display the local clock of any chosen city (e.g. Tokyo, London, New York) or simulate day/night lighting cycles for a different hemisphere without altering your PC's real clock.

  2. International Outreach & Client Work:

    • Localize browser profiles, CRM tools, scheduling calendars, Slack, Discord, or web apps to match client timezones, avoiding timezone math errors while keeping your taskbar clock accurate.

  3. Software Testing & QA:

    • Verify application behavior across global regions (e.g., date-boundary logic, DST shifts, calendar schedulers, daily reset intervals) on demand.

  4. Privacy & Anti-Fingerprinting:

    • Mask your real physical timezone from web tracking scripts and telemetry engines that cross-check timezone offsets.

Important Usage Notes

  • Adding Custom Applications: By default, ZoneShift targets Wallpaper Engine processes to keep other apps unaffected out of the box. To target any other application (browsers, chat apps, games, etc.):

    1. Open the Windhawk UI.
    2. Navigate to ZoneShift -> Details -> Advanced tab.
    3. Under Process inclusion list, add the executable name (e.g., chrome.exe, slack.exe, yourapp.exe).
    4. Click Save.

  • Web Wallpapers and Time Shifting: Chromium/CEF web wallpapers evaluate local time via ICU using the spoofed TimeZoneKeyName and UTC time. To apply an artificial minute offset in web wallpapers, enable Shift UTC Time.

  • UTC Time Shifting in Browsers: Enabling Shift UTC Time shifts GetSystemTime. Note that shifting UTC time by more than a few minutes in web browsers may cause HTTPS security certificate validation failures, expired cookies, or invalid TOTP two-factor authentication codes. Keep this option disabled unless specifically required.

  • Client Games & Anti-Cheat: Many multiplayer games employ anti-cheat systems that inspect or block process hooks. Use caution when injecting mods into protected games, and note that server-authoritative games determine daily resets on the game server.

How It Works

Windows apps query time through multiple Win32, NT, ICU, CRT, and registry APIs. ZoneShift intercepts all critical layers at the process level:

  • GetDynamicTimeZoneInformation & GetTimeZoneInformation: Modern Win32 APIs used by Chromium, Electron, CEF, Node.js, and ICU to resolve IANA and Windows timezones.
  • GetLocalTime: Native API called by C++/DirectX apps, desktop widgets, and Wallpaper Engine scene wallpapers.
  • SystemTimeToTzSpecificLocalTime[Ex] / TzSpecificLocalTimeToSystemTime[Ex]: Local-to-UTC and UTC-to-local conversions with full dynamic Daylight Saving Time (DST) support.
  • FileTimeToLocalFileTime / LocalFileTimeToFileTime: File and timestamp conversions.
  • NtQuerySystemInformation (SystemTimeOfDayInformation): Low-level NT kernel time-of-day bias.
  • RegQueryValueExW: Intercepts TimeZoneKeyName and ActiveTimeBias queries.
  • Windows ICU Integration: Automatically converts any IANA identifier (e.g. Europe/Warsaw, America/Mexico_City, Asia/Tokyo) to Windows time zones using icu.dll.

Source Code & Support

Source code, issue tracker, and documentation: GitHub Repository

entry.title: Quick Share Tile 1.0.0
entry.content:
Quick Share Tile

Replace the Windows 11 Nearby sharing Quick Settings tile with a Quick Share launcher.

Keep your Quick Settings layout intact while giving the native Nearby sharing tile a new purpose.

Preview

Features

  • Replaces the Nearby sharing tile with Quick Share.
  • Changes the tile's name and icon.
  • Preserves native tile dimensions, position and styling.
  • Launches Quick Share with a single click.
  • Automatically restores the original tile when disabled.

Requirements

  • Windows 11 x64, build 24H2 or later (Quick Settings hosted by ShellHost.exe).

  • Windhawk.

  • Google's Quick Share for Windows installed (not Samsung's app of the same name).

  • Quick Share shortcut located at:

    C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Quick Share.lnk

Settings

Native tile to replace

The accessibility name of the tile to replace.

Default: Nearby sharing

The name is language-dependent. Change it if your Windows installation uses another display language.

Log the visual tree

Logs the Quick Settings visual tree for troubleshooting.

Known Limitations

  • Tested on Windows 11 x64 build 26300.
  • Other Windows builds are not guaranteed to work.
  • The tile's active appearance still reflects Nearby sharing, not Quick Share's actual running state.
  • The Quick Share shortcut path is currently hardcoded.
  • This mod launches Quick Share; it does not implement Quick Share functionality.

Credits

Parts of the ControlCenter.dll hooking and cleanup logic are based on refined-quick-settings-and-sound (GPL-3.0-only). This mod is therefore also released under GPL-3.0-only.

Uninstallation

Disable or remove the mod through Windhawk.

The original Nearby sharing tile is restored, including its label, icon, click behavior and keyboard navigation.

entry.title: System Tray BreakTimer 0.1.8
entry.content:
System Tray BreakTimer

Each time you enable the mod, it starts paused. Click P in the notification area to start. Windows can place new icons in the tray overflow.

S means Standby until the next whole clock minute. A fresh interval started at exactly :00 begins immediately. With the default 15-minute interval, starting at 1:01:25 shows S until 1:02:00. The tray shows 2 at 1:15:59, then 60 in the seconds color at 1:16:00. It counts down to 1 in seconds. Set Start seconds countdown to any value from 5 to 60 seconds. For example, at 10 seconds the tray shows 1 minute until 1:16:50. The break starts at 1:17:00 and lasts one minute by default. B means a break is in progress. Hover over the icon for the unit, time remaining and pause reason. Both minutes and seconds use bold numerals in your chosen tray colors.

The borderless break window has a Skip Break button and a gauge-colored X in its upper-right corner. Both end the break silently and start a fresh work interval with the usual Standby. The gauge scales to 90% of the shorter usable monitor dimension. With multiple windows, one action applies to them all. To skip with the keyboard, Alt+Tab to the break window marked B and press Enter on Skip Break.

Tray commands

A single left-click toggles pause. Pausing discards the current interval, and unpausing starts a fresh one. Turn on Require a double-click to pause or unpause if you prefer. Keyboard activation still takes one press. Right-click the tray icon to open its menu.

When the tray shows P, the menu contains only Unpause. During S / Standby or B / On break, the menu contains only Pause. During the work countdown, including its final seconds, the menu has three commands.

  • Skip to next break starts a break immediately. Its end schedules a fresh work interval.
  • Reset ends the current phase and starts a fresh work interval.
  • Pause discards the current countdown, closes any break windows and leaves the mod paused indefinitely until you unpause it. When you unpause, S appears until the next whole minute, then the entire Break every interval begins. At exactly :00 it starts immediately.

Sound — In Settings, Play wind chimes is on by default. The default audio device plays one short chime for each of these two events.

  • The tray countdown reaches zero and a scheduled break begins.
  • The gauge reaches 00:00 and the break finishes naturally.

Choosing Skip to next break starts the break silently. It still chimes if the gauge reaches zero. Skip Break, X, Reset, Pause and Unpause are silent. Each event plays its cue once across all monitors. Turning sound off also stops a cue already playing.

The bundled wind chime was recorded by GnoteSoundz and is available under CC0 1.0. To use your own recording, browse to a local WAV under Custom sound file (optional). Choose uncompressed 8- or 16-bit PCM, mono or stereo, at 8–48 kHz, up to 10 seconds and 2 MiB. An empty field or an unreadable or unsupported file uses the bundled chime. On Windhawk 1.x, you can paste a quoted path copied from Explorer. If you replace the WAV at the same path, switch sound off and back on to load it again.

Settings — Open the mod's Details, then Settings. Windhawk 2.0 alpha 8 shows break durations as minute sliders and includes a file browser. Windhawk 1.x uses numeric fields for durations and a text field for the WAV path. If Break every is below twice Break for, the timer uses twice the break length. For example, a 25-minute break and a 40-minute interval give 50 minutes of work. Changes to durations apply on the next fresh interval or break. Appearance changes take effect immediately. Set Background opacity under Tray icon to 0% for a transparent background or to 100% for a solid color. After an update, the saved opacity slider value controls the background. Windows controls whether the full-screen pause banner appears. The timer pauses independently of banner delivery.

Automatic pauses

After five idle minutes during work or Standby, the icon shows P. The timer starts a fresh Break every interval when you return. Ordinary idle time during a break lets the gauge run to zero.

Locking or disconnecting the session, suspending the PC, or entering full screen with auto-pause enabled also pauses the timer. If a break is in progress, its window closes silently. When the last pause reason clears, the icon shows S until the next whole minute, then starts the full work interval. At exactly :00 it starts immediately. For example, unlocking at 2:04:20 starts the default 15-minute work interval at 2:05, with the next break at 2:20.

A manual pause lasts until you choose Unpause. Choosing Unpause also overrides a current idle or full-screen pause. An unavailable Windows session must reconnect, unlock or wake before a new interval can begin.

Full-screen auto-pause and its optional banner both default to off. With auto-pause off, the break window can appear over a game or presentation and may interrupt exclusive full screen. Enable Auto-pause for full-screen apps to pause the timer while a full-screen app is detected.

Inspired by Stretchly. Functionality inspiration only. No code was reused.

entry.title: Snap Groups: Alt+Tab and taskbar 0.5.3
entry.content:
Snap Groups: Alt+Tab and taskbar

Keep native Snap Groups in Alt+Tab and give each group a separate taskbar button with a grid of its application icons. Individual member buttons can be hidden; windows outside groups remain accessible.

Usage

Enable Snap windows and the option to show snapped groups in Alt+Tab under Windows Settings > System > Multitasking. Arrange at least two windows into a native Snap Group. The mod reads groups maintained by Windows.

A group button brings all members forward. With the default click setting, clicking an active group minimizes it. If a member is already minimized, the button restores the group. Closing a group button minimizes the group by default and does not close the applications. Group buttons are temporary and cannot be pinned; ordinary pinned application launchers remain.

The taskbar label uses the native localized group title. Hover previews use the Windows group visual. Win+Tab is unchanged. Group commands use native Windows activation/minimization; animation behavior follows those native commands.

Settings

  • Independently enable Alt+Tab filtering, group taskbar buttons and hiding of individual member buttons.
  • Keep separate buttons for separate groups, including groups of the same apps.
  • Display two to four equally sized icons in a two-column grid. Adjust icon size, spacing and incomplete-row alignment. The icon limit does not limit membership.
  • Order icons by screen rows from top to bottom and centers from left to right. A tall window belongs to its first row (default), or use Windows' member order. Minimized windows use restored positions; only icon order changes.
  • Choose restore-only or minimize-if-active behavior, and the close-button action.
  • Adjust refresh interval and current-virtual-desktop filtering.
  • Enable or disable native hover previews.
  • Diagnostic mode keeps individual Alt+Tab cards and disables taskbar integration.

Tested configuration and limitations

Version 0.5.2 was tested on Windows 11 25H2 (26200.8246, x64), Windhawk 1.7.3: Alt+Tab advancement, group activity and no empty buttons after disable/enable; group recovery, native previews, Alt+Tab/activity and minimize/restore after Explorer restart; group creation on the other monitor. Separate classic/modern preview routes were not independently identified. The support-trace toggle and heavy-game scenario below were confirmed on 0.4.24, not repeated for 0.5.x.

  • Independent taskbar per monitor 1.7.0: group creation, moving groups between monitors and restoring minimized groups; no empty buttons or unload stalls in the tested disable/enable scenario.
  • Alt+Tab per monitor 1.2.1: switching during a heavy game and after closing it, including disabling both mods without restarting Explorer.

Taskbar integration calls native DLL methods and COM interfaces; it does not parse machine instructions or read private task-list/preview object fields. Native task items come from the shell enumerator. Hidden members and pending button restores use owned window icons until their own task list is restored. Native previews replace the window thumbnail factory for owned group proxies; Windows creates and manages the visual itself. Required shell symbols must be available. Missing optional preview/selection methods leave those paths native. Shell interfaces are undocumented; other Windows versions and DLL revisions remain unverified, and updates can require changes to the mod. Longer sessions and other monitor/DPI/virtual desktop configurations have limited coverage. ARM64 installation is allowed; ARM64 runtime behavior is unverified.

Report mod problems in https://github.com/ramensoftware/windhawk-mods/issues. Include "hide-snapped" in the title and mention @coldfeudal in the report.

Diagnostics and removal

Windhawk debug logging records phase codes and counts without window/document titles. Disable this mod to restore the native taskbar and switcher behavior. Enable Record support trace only when collecting diagnostics. Changing this setting reloads the mod. Bounded journals are stored in Windhawk's per-mod storage directory, in the traces subfolder. A background writer saves queued records. Records may be dropped under load. Journals contain numeric identities, counts and stack/module information, without window titles or AppID strings.

The Alt+Tab scoping approach was informed by Alt+Tab per monitor.

entry.title: Windows 11 IME Tray Icon Fix 1.0
entry.content:
Windows 11 IME Tray Icon Fix

Default Stock Layout And The Bug

  Screen Left  <-----------------------------------------------------  Screen Right Edge
  [Chevron ^]  |  [SysPager (Tray Icons)]  |  [IME Indicator]  |  [Clock]  |  [Show Desktop]

The notification area (TrayNotifyWnd) is anchored to the right edge of the screen, while child windows are laid out left-to-right. Notice that the IME Indicator sits right in the middle, between the third-party tray icons (SysPager) and the clock.

When "Let me set a different input method for each app window" is enabled in a multilingual setup (e.g., English, Chinese, Japanese):

  1. While typing in an app, the indicator often displays 2 glyphs (e.g., CH + 中 or JP + あ), occupying a wider slot.
  2. When you click a tray icon (such as Steam or WiFi), WM_LBUTTONDOWN immediately shifts focus to explorer.exe.
  3. The shell defaults to English, shrinking the indicator down to 1 glyph (ENG).
  4. Because the clock on the right is pinned to the right edge, the shrunk width forces everything to the left of the indicator (SysPager and Chevron ^) to slide rightward.
  5. When WM_LBUTTONUP fires, the icon you aimed at has moved, and your click lands on whichever neighboring icon slid under your cursor.

The Fix

[IME Indicator]  |  [Chevron ^]  |  [SysPager (Tray Icons)]  |  [Clock]  |  [Show Desktop]

The indicator takes the first slot and everything that used to sit left of it moves right by the indicator's width. Thus, every band is now to the right of the indicator, sits at a fixed distance from the right edge and never moves.

Mimicking Docked Language Bar?

Yes. But the docked language bar is broken in win10 (unstable, and won't work in remote desktop - even if you enable this option in both sides, and the latest MSPY doesn't support it unless you turn on "Use the old version of MSPY") and is completely removed in win11.

Notes and known limitations

  • This mod is separated from the Win 10 fix because the UI technology (XAML vs Win32) is completely different. So they share no common code.
  • No alternative modes. You can adjust width / hide icon using the official (m417z) mods "Taskbar height and icon size" and "Taskbar tray system icon tweaks".
  • This mod alters the grid columns (indice), which might be changed by other mods too (Styler). The co-existence itself is fine, but recording the correct state (for editing settings / turning on or off on-the-fly) across multiple mods is techniclaly impossible. It's recommended to use one mod alone, if you need both, create a custom style theme with the icons swapped.
  • Source code and reverse engineering credit goes to AI bot (hy4). Heavily guided to follow the framework of the official mods above, with AI-hallucinated overhead (it added a repeating timer) dropped. But not fully revised (don't want to learn XAML 🙂).
  • SystemTrayFrameGrid can be a Grid or a StackPanel. Verified on Windows 11 24H2 LTSC (Grid) and 26H2 (StackPanel). Other versions should work as the mechanism is identical and the Windhawk should handle the injection properly, remain untested though.

entry.title: SMTC Now Playing Desktop Widgets 1.0.11
entry.content:
SMTC Now Playing Desktop Widgets

Displays up to 5 customizable, multi-monitor Now Playing widgets on your Windows 11 desktop using the native Windows System Media Transport Controls (SMTC) API.

When album art is unavailable, the widgets display an embedded default image.

Themes

  • Standard: Wide horizontal Acrylic card with rounded album art, bold track/artist text, 5 outlined playback controls, and a progress bar with timestamps.
  • Album: Full-bleed dimmed album art square with centered track/artist text, corner timestamps, and a bottom-edge progress bar.
  • Cardstock: Vertical portrait Acrylic card with full-brightness album art, centered track/artist, and progress bar. Automatically shrinks uniformly when playback controls are disabled.
  • Simplified: Sleek single-row horizontal Acrylic bar with compact art, track/artist text, 5 outlined playback controls, and a clean progress bar without timestamps.

Usage

  • Move Widgets: Left-click and drag any widget across any monitor (unless "Lock Position" is enabled for that instance). Coordinates save automatically.
  • Display-Only Mode: Enable "Disable Playback Controls" on any instance to hide all transport buttons and disable progress bar seeking.

entry.title: Windows Hello Auto OK 0.1.3
entry.content:
Windows Hello Auto OK

Confirms the ready OK button in standard Windows Hello biometric dialogs, regardless of the requesting application or interface language.

Illustrated demo using an English interface and the display name User.

Detection uses AutomationId, control types, visibility and enabled state. It never matches captions, translated messages, account names or websites. Visible dialogs owned by the Windows CredentialUIBroker are monitored directly, only while the Hello dialog itself is the foreground window. Visible credential input fields prevent automatic confirmation.

This removes Windows Hello's manual confirmation step: a program requesting verification can be approved as soon as Windows recognizes you, provided its Hello dialog is active. Background dialogs are never confirmed automatically.

The mod runs inside CredentialUIBroker.exe, with no helper process or UAC launcher. It reacts to window events and checks readiness only while its dialog is active. No credential values, account names, or biometric data are read.

This is an experimental release. Its readiness check describes the standard Windows Hello UI structure, not an independent biometric-success API. Windows still performs authentication. Custom application dialogs and future changes to the system UI may require an update.

entry.title: Edge No Bleed 1.0.0
entry.content:
Edge No Bleed

Eliminates the persistent 1-2px margin gap where desktop wallpaper bleeds through along screen edges behind maximized windows.

The Problem

On Windows 10 and 11, users running dark-mode themes, IDEs, terminals, and browsers frequently notice a razor-thin 1-2px strip of desktop wallpaper leaking through along the edges of maximized windows (especially at the bottom or side monitor borders).

Why This Happens

  • DWM Frame Padding & Fractional DPI Rounding: Windows calculates maximized client coordinates by converting logical device-independent units into physical screen pixels. At fractional display scaling factors (such as 125%, 150%, or 175%), rounding calculations frequently leave a 1-2 physical pixel deficit against the work area, exposing bright desktop wallpaper pixels.
  • Invisible Margin Bounds: Normal Win32 maximized frames hang invisible resize margins off-screen, but custom-chrome and modern applications (such as Chromium, Electron, and Windows Terminal) size their own frames and can fall short of physical display boundaries.

How It Works

Edge No Bleed runs as a dedicated tool mod within Windhawk without injecting invasive hooks into third-party processes. It monitors window position and state changes via out-of-context WinEvents on a dedicated message-loop worker thread:

  1. When a window is maximized, the mod measures its true visible frame bounds using DwmGetWindowAttribute(DWMWA_EXTENDED_FRAME_BOUNDS) against the monitor's work area (MONITORINFO::rcWork).
  2. If a 1-2px fractional rounding gap is detected, the mod expands the window frame via SetWindowPos by the exact measured discrepancy, sealing the edge flush against the screen.
  3. If an auto-hide taskbar is active on that edge, the mod detects it via SHAppBarMessage(ABM_GETAUTOHIDEBAREX) and preserves the 1px mouse-hover reveal strip.

Comparison With Other Mods

  • Maximized Window Margins: That mod intentionally adds large margins (10px to 200px, macOS-style) by shrinking the system work area with AppBars. Edge No Bleed does the opposite: it eliminates unwanted 1-2px fractional DPI gaps so maximized windows sit completely flush.
  • Classic Maximized Windows Fix: That mod is exclusively designed for the legacy Classic 3D Theme on Windows 10/11 using region clipping (SetWindowRgn). Edge No Bleed targets standard modern DWM themes and dark-mode setups.

entry.title: Start Menu Groups 1.0.0
entry.content:
Start Menu Groups

Add your own app groups to the Windows 11 Start menu, before or after the Pinned section (or in place of the built‑in All → View: Category grid), using the same look as Start: rounded tiles with an icon preview, an overflow cluster for the remaining apps and the group name underneath.

Designed for the Windows 11 Start menu (StartMenuExperienceHost.exe).

Features

  • Your own groups — create any number of groups and put any Start menu app in them, desktop and Store apps alike. An app can be in several groups.
  • Apps, programs and websites — each item is a Start app (picked by name or app ID), a program, file or folder (full path with optional arguments), or a website opened in the default browser.
  • Custom names and icons — every item can have its own label and icon: an .ico, .exe, .dll or image file, an image link (such as a website's favicon), a Fluent icon by its code (e.g. E774) or an emoji.
  • Native look — rounded tiles, borders and colors match Start's own category view and follow the Windows light / dark theme.
  • Resizable tiles — give each group its own tile size, from 1 × 1 up to 6 × 4 (24 apps). Bigger tiles take more cells of the group grid. A 1 × 1 tile is a single app on its own, without a group.
  • Overflow cluster — when a group has more apps than fit, the last cell shows the rest as small icons; click it to open the whole group.
  • Right‑click menu — right‑click an app in a group for Edit, Run as administrator, Open file location, Pin to taskbar, App settings and Uninstall, like Start's own apps.
  • Size presets — Default, Small and Large presets for the tiles, icons and names, plus control over gaps, corner radius, colors and group names.
  • Placement — show the groups before or after Pinned, after Recommended / Recent, or after the All section, with an optional section title.
  • Hide Start's sections — optionally hide Start's own Pinned, Recommended and All sections and use only your groups.
  • Settings window — right‑click the groups in Start → Customize Start Groups for a visual editor with drag & drop (see Settings window).
  • Import / export — all settings can be exported to and imported from a JSON file.

Screenshots

The settings window, with drag & drop editing of groups and apps:

Setting it up

Everything is configured on the mod's Settings tab in Windhawk, in sections:

  • Groups — add a group with Add new item, give it a name, a tile size and its items. For a Start app, enter the app's name exactly as it appears in Start (for example Calculator, Visual Studio Code; case doesn't matter), or its app ID (AUMID, such as Microsoft.WindowsCalculator_8wekyb3d8bbwe!App). For a program, its full path (a program, file or folder) and optional arguments; for a website, its address. Reorder groups with the arrows.
  • Behavior — where the groups appear, the section title, app names and tooltips, sorting, empty groups, the number of columns when a group is opened, and hiding Start's own sections.
  • Tiles, Icons, Group names — sizes, gaps and colors. The defaults match Start's own category view.

Changes apply to Start as soon as you click Save settings.

Settings window

Right‑click the groups in Start → Customize Start Groups (also added to Start's own right‑click menu, after Start settings) opens a settings window with the same settings, but easier to edit:

  • Groups — shows the groups the way Start does. Drag apps to reorder them or move them to another group, drag a tile to reorder the groups, drag a tile's corner to resize it, and drag apps from the All Apps list onto a tile to add them. The selected group and app are edited below the groups. Right‑click a tile to rename, duplicate or delete it.
  • Customization — the size preset (Default, Small, Large), gaps, corner radius, colors and group names.
  • Behavior — placement, section title, app names, tooltips, sorting and columns.
  • Built‑in sections — hide Start's own Pinned, Recommended and All sections.

Start apps are picked by name with suggestions from the apps in Start; programs have a file picker. Groups and items can be duplicated, and an app can be added on its own, without a group. Import / Export at the bottom of the navigation pane save all settings to, or load them from, a JSON file.

The window is hosted by File Explorer — the mod also loads into explorer.exe for this, and does nothing else there — because the Start menu process can't host one. It edits the same settings as Windhawk. Windhawk keeps them in a protected registry key, so Save shows an administrator (UAC) prompt for Windows PowerShell, which imports the new settings, and Start updates right after. The import checks that the settings file is exactly the one the window wrote, so no other program can change what gets saved. If the settings were changed in Windhawk while the window was open, Save asks before replacing them. The portable version of Windhawk isn't supported by the window.

Tile size and apps in the tile

Each group has two size settings:

  • Tile size — width × height of the tile, in app spots. 2 × 2 is the size of one of Start's own tiles; 1 × 1 is an app on its own, without a group.
  • Apps in the tile — apps per row × rows of apps, at most the tile size. Default fills the tile with one app per spot; the rest go in the overflow cluster.

A group can also hide its app names, its group name, or its tile background (no background, border or padding — just the apps, e.g. for a single app on its own).

Colors

Colors are #RRGGBB or #AARRGGBB. Leave a color empty to follow the Windows theme and match Start.

Network access

The mod doesn't connect to the internet by itself, and the default settings don't contact any server: the default websites show a globe icon.

An icon set to an image link (http:// or https://, such as a website's favicon) is downloaded from that address by Windows' XAML image loader: a normal web request for the image, which sends your IP address and a user agent to that server. It happens when Start builds the tiles (when the mod loads, on a theme or settings change, and when a group is opened), and when the settings window shows the item. To avoid it, leave the icon empty or use a local file, a Fluent icon code or an emoji.

Compatibility

The mod reaches Start's UI directly, without XAML diagnostics, so it works alongside mods and tools that use them, such as Windows 11 Start Menu Styler.

Language

The groups are placed next to Start's pinned list, found by its element name, so they show in any display language. Two things go by Start's English titles: hiding Start's sections (Pinned, Recommended / Recent, All), and adding Customize Start Groups after Start settings in Start's own right‑click menu. In other languages, open the settings window by right‑clicking the groups instead.

Default configuration

Out of the box the mod adds these groups before the Pinned section, under an Apps heading:

  • Group 1 — Microsoft Store, Settings, Notepad, Weather
  • Group 2 — Camera, Paint, Calculator, Calendar
  • Favorites — Photos, Terminal, Notepad, Get Help (group name hidden)
  • Group 3 (3 × 3) — Sound Recorder, Voice access, Task Manager, Movies & TV, File Explorer, Sticky Notes
  • System (3 × 1) — Control Panel, Services, Run (group name hidden)
  • Websites (3 × 2) — YouTube, ChatGPT, Example, Google, Reddit, dan13.me

Empty groups are hidden. None of Start's own sections are hidden by default. Everything is configurable in the mod settings.

entry.title: Text Capitalization 0.3.1
entry.content:
Text Capitalization

Select text and press Ctrl+Alt+P to capture the selection and open a compact picker. The selected text is shown in a read-only preview; Up/Down changes the highlighted case and updates the preview. Enter or clicking a case replaces the original selection with the transformed text. Escape cancels.

Default shortcuts are Ctrl+Alt+P (open picker), Ctrl+Alt+C (apply saved case immediately), Up/Down (navigate), Enter (apply highlighted case), and Escape (cancel). Shortcuts are configurable in Windhawk settings. On older Windhawk versions enter numeric VK values such as ctrl+alt+80 for Ctrl+Alt+P.

The picker never takes keyboard focus from the original editor. Selection capture and replacement use a guarded clipboard copy/paste workflow instead of depending on UI Automation selection detection. The clipboard is snapshotted and restoration is best-effort. The mode is remembered in Windhawk local storage.

Compatibility depends on the target app supporting copy and paste and leaving the original selection intact while the non-activating picker is shown. Elevated apps may reject simulated input if Windhawk/Explorer runs at a lower integrity level.

entry.title: Explorer Default Folder 1.0.0
entry.content:
Explorer Default Folder

Opens every new File Explorer window or tab in a folder of your choice when it would otherwise open This PC, Home or Quick access.

Enter a folder in the mod settings, for example D:\Documents, %USERPROFILE%\Downloads, ~\Downloads, Downloads or shell:Downloads. Environment variables are expanded, and ~ or a relative path starts at your user folder. Leave the setting empty to keep Explorer's normal behavior.

You can apply the folder to new windows only, new tabs only, or both, and optionally reopen the folder you closed most recently instead.

Windows and tabs opened for any other folder are not changed, and navigating to This PC or Home yourself in an existing tab is not redirected. A new window or tab that is explicitly opened at This PC or Home (for example with the This PC desktop icon) can't be told apart from a default one, so it is redirected too.

How it works

The mod listens to Shell window events instead of polling, so it costs nothing while idle and redirects a new tab as soon as its first location loads. Its background thread never holds up Explorer's windows, even when the folder is on a slow or offline network share.

Compatibility

Designed for File Explorer on Windows 10 and 11. It uses documented Shell COM interfaces rather than version-specific Explorer symbols, so it does not need an update for each Explorer build.

entry.title: File Explorer navigation pane: thin divider, even padding 1.0
entry.content:
File Explorer navigation pane: thin divider, even padding

A set of small adjustments of the navigation pane of File Explorer: the tree of folders on the left of a folder window. Every adjustment has a setting, and can be changed or turned off.

Before and after

The pin icons are set to 10% opacity in this screenshot, and the pointer is on the folder Data (D:), which shows the expand arrows. The left half is without the mod, the right half is with the mod.

What it does

  • Thin divider. The strip between the navigation pane and the files area is replaced with a line of 1 pixel. By default, the line has the color of the line below the command bar, for the light and for the dark theme. The color is configurable. The navigation pane can still be resized by dragging the divider.
  • Even padding. The gap to the left of the items of the navigation pane is made the same as the gap to the right of them. The size is configurable. A space above and below the contents of the navigation pane can be added too.
  • Pin icons. The pin icons to the right of the pinned folders can be made less visible, with a configurable opacity, or hidden.
  • Separators. The lines which separate the groups of the navigation pane can be made longer or shorter. They can go from edge to edge.
  • Expand arrows. The arrows can be moved vertically.

Defaults

The divider, the padding, the pin icons and the offset of the arrows are adjusted by default. To get the stock look of a part back, use these values:

  • Thin divider: off.
  • Padding of the navigation pane: -1.
  • Vertical padding of the navigation pane: 0.
  • Hide the pin icons: off, with the opacity of 0.
  • Vertical offset of the expand arrows: 0.

The adjustment of the separators is turned off by default.

Other mods

The thin divider and the padding have no counterpart in other mods. For the rest, there are mods which do related things in a different way:

  • Explorer TreeItem Tweaker and Classic Explorer Treeview can hide the pin icons. This mod can also fade them instead of hiding them.
  • Explorer TreeLine Killer hides the separators and changes the spacing around them. This mod keeps the separators and changes their length.
  • Explorer Navigation Tree Offset shifts the tree and can remove the expand arrows. This mod moves the arrows vertically by a pixel or two.

The mods can be used together. A part of this mod which is set to its stock value does nothing at all, so if another mod takes care of the pin icons, the separators or the arrows, set that part to the stock value here, as listed above. The combinations with those mods weren't tested.

The files area of a folder window is handled by a separate mod, File Explorer List view indent fix and files area spacing.

Scaling and themes

The padding and the side gaps of the separators follow the display scaling. The offset of the expand arrows is a small correction, and is applied in physical pixels regardless of the scaling.

The mod was only tested with a single monitor. With several monitors of different scaling, the side gaps of the separators can be off on a monitor whose scaling differs from the one of the main monitor. A folder window which was moved to such a monitor can also keep the adjusted padding after the mod is turned off, until it's reopened.

The automatic color of the thin divider is chosen when a folder window is opened. Windows which are already open when the theme changes keep the old color until they're reopened. The divider is left alone in the high contrast mode.

Other programs

By default, the mod only applies to File Explorer (explorer.exe). That's the recommended setup, and nothing has to be configured for it.

The same navigation pane is used by the Open/Save dialogs of other programs. To adjust it there too, add the programs to the custom process inclusion list in the Advanced tab of the mod, by the name of the executable file, for example notepad.exe. explorer.exe doesn't have to be added, it's always included.

It's also possible to add *, which means all programs. The mod is then loaded into every process, including the ones which never show a file dialog, so adding only the programs you need is the lighter option.

Only 64-bit programs are supported. In a program other than File Explorer, the mod does nothing until the program loads explorerframe.dll, which usually happens when a file dialog is opened for the first time. From then on, the vertical offset of the expand arrows applies to all tree views of that program.

How it works

The divider and the padding are properties of DirectUI elements of the frame of a folder window. They're changed when a frame is created, and the windows which are already open are adjusted when the mod is loaded. The functions which are exported by dui70.dll are used for that. The adjustments are only made to elements which have the expected stock values.

The pin icons are the state images of the tree of the navigation pane. The mod gives the tree a copy of its state image list with faded images, and leaves the list of File Explorer itself untouched.

The separators are adjusted while File Explorer draws them, which relies on the debug symbols of explorerframe.dll. If that part can't be set up on a Windows build, the rest of the mod still works. The expand arrows are moved while they're drawn with the theme of a tree view.

No files are modified. When the mod is turned off, the stock look is restored.

Tested on Windows 11 build 26300 (26H2 preview) at 125% scaling, with the light and the dark theme.

entry.title: Frosted Window Blur 1.0.0
entry.content:
Frosted Window Blur

Give any window a frosted glass look, like the Windows 11 Settings app: what's behind the window is blurred, and you choose how strong the blur is for each window.

The same Notepad window with the blur off, at level 1 and at level 3.

Usage

  • Ctrl + Shift + mouse wheel down over any window: more blur
  • Ctrl + Shift + mouse wheel up: less blur (the lowest step turns it off)
  • Ctrl + Shift + middle-click over a window: blur off

Every window keeps its own blur level, and the blur stays the same when you click into another window. A small "Blur 2/3" indicator shows up briefly after every change.

The key combination can be changed in the settings. The default doesn't use Alt, so it doesn't clash with mods that use Alt + wheel or Ctrl + Alt + wheel (for example to change opacity).

There's also an optional small button next to the minimize button of the active window (off by default): left-click = next blur level (wraps back to off), right-click = blur off.

The maximum level, the window's own opacity while blurred, the indicator, the button and excluded programs can all be changed in the mod settings, and the changes apply instantly. When the mod is disabled or unloaded, the blur is removed from every window and their opacity is restored.

How it works

  • The window itself isn't changed, except that it's made a bit see-through (75% by default) so the blur behind it shows. Windows that are already see-through (for example made so by another mod) keep their own opacity.
  • The blur is drawn by helper windows of the mod that have no content of their own and only the DWM blur-behind effect. They sit directly behind the window in the z-order and follow it when it's moved, resized, minimized, restored, hidden or brought to the front. They never take focus and can't be clicked, so the blur doesn't turn off when the window loses focus.
  • Windows' blur has a fixed radius, so every level stacks one more blur pass behind the window, which makes it noticeably stronger.
  • It's fully event driven (SetWinEventHook, no polling timer), so it uses no CPU while nothing moves. Higher levels on large windows cost a bit more GPU.
  • The wheel shortcut uses a keyboard hook that only arms a mouse hook while the modifier keys are held down. Both hooks run on their own thread that only forwards events. Over excluded programs, the taskbar and the desktop, the shortcut is passed through as usual.
  • The mod runs in its own dedicated windhawk.exe process (a "tool mod"), so it doesn't inject into Explorer or any other program.

Limitations

  • Windows of programs running as administrator (for example Task Manager or Windhawk's own window) can't be changed, because Windows blocks a normal program from modifying them (UIPI). Windows that draw their own transparency are left alone too.
  • While a window is dragged, the blur can trail a frame behind it.
  • If another mod also blurs the same window, the effects add up.

entry.title: File Copy Progress Bar Styles 1.0.0
entry.content:
File Copy Progress Bar Styles

Restyles the progress bar shown in the Windows file copy / move / delete dialog, and the extraction progress bar of 7-Zip and WinRAR.

Screenshots of the styles are shown below.

Accent styles (use the accent color)

  • Solid - flat color

  • Satin - gradient with a top highlight

  • Candy Cane - diagonal stripes

  • Neon Tube - dark track with a glowing core

  • Arcade - retro blocks

Designer styles (fixed colors, some with their own track)

  • Evergreen - dark green timeline with stepped bands and a diamond knob

  • Sorbet - pink, yellow and blue segments

  • Polka - blue gradient with dot markers

  • Aurora - cyan-to-lilac gradient with an end marker and tick track

  • Ember - orange diagonal stripes on a striped gray track

  • Mint - soft green bar with a subtle bottom shade

  • Fire & Ice - red-to-icy-blue gradient

  • Prism - full-spectrum gradient

  • Confetti - colorful mosaic

  • Carbon - dark mosaic on a dark track

  • Dusk - navy-to-orange-to-lilac gradient

Paused and error states automatically switch to amber and red.

Notes

  • Only the copy dialog is restyled by default. The drive usage bars in This PC keep the standard Windows look. Turn on "Also restyle other progress bars in Explorer" to restyle those too.
  • The mod also loads into 7-Zip (7zG.exe, 7zFM.exe) and WinRAR (WinRAR.exe) and restyles their extraction progress bars. To turn that off, switch off "Also style 7-Zip and WinRAR" in the settings (or add those processes to the mod's custom process exclusion list in the Advanced tab). Extracting a ZIP with Explorer's built-in "Extract All" uses the normal copy dialog.
  • Tested on Windows 11. The theme lookup uses an undocumented uxtheme function (ordinal 74), so other Windows versions have not been verified.
  • In a dark copy dialog the tracks of the styles are darkened to match.
  • Windows itself turns a drive bar red when the drive has under 10% free.
  • Copy dialogs shown by other processes (for example inside an app's Open/Save dialog) are not styled. Add those processes in the mod's custom process inclusion list.
  • Setting changes show up the next time the bar repaints.
  • To troubleshoot, enable logging in the mod's Advanced tab and watch the log during a copy.

entry.title: Windows Border Switch 1.2.1
entry.content:
Windows Border Switch

English · Русский

Windows Border Switch hides system-drawn borders around windows and panels in Windows 11.

Features
Setting Controls
Active window The focused window's system border or its title bar accent color
Inactive windows System borders of windows without focus
Dialogs System borders of classic Win32 dialogs, with or without focus
Taskbar The taskbar edge and the virtual desktops strip at the bottom of Task View
Start menu The Start menu and its Phone Link panel
Search The Windows Search panel
Notifications The notification center, calendar, and notification banners on the desktop
Quick Settings Quick Settings and the media controls above them
Keyboard layout The outer border of the keyboard layout selector
Widgets The outer border of the Widgets board
Exceptions Keep the usual border and title bar for active, inactive, or all windows of selected apps

The interface is available in English, Russian, Spanish, German, Brazilian Portuguese, and Simplified Chinese.

Limitations

  • Shell borders depend on the Windows build and Windows Web Experience Pack. After enabling or updating the mod, some panels may require restarting Windows Explorer or signing out and back in.
  • Apps running as administrator, including Windhawk, may retain their borders. Apps that draw their own frames control their appearance.

Platforms

Requires Windows 11 x64 or ARM64.

Compatibility

The following mods overlap with Windows Border Switch for application window borders:

  • Invisible Window Borders — also hides system-drawn window borders.
  • Windows 11 Accent Window Border — sets window border colors, which can conflict with hiding those borders.

Do not use multiple mods to control the same window border or title bar: they can override each other's settings and exceptions. To use either mod for window borders and Windows Border Switch only for shell panels, set Active window, Inactive windows, and Dialogs to Windows-defined in Windows Border Switch.

The following Styler mods customize shell panels. Their themes and custom rules may also change borders:

  • Windows 11 Start Menu Styler — styles the Start menu and Search panel (styling guide).
  • Windows 11 Taskbar Styler — styles the taskbar, including its edge (styling guide).
  • Windows 11 Notification Center Styler — styles notifications, the calendar, Quick Settings, and media controls (styling guide).

If a theme or rule controls the same border, set the corresponding Windows Border Switch option to Windows-defined, or remove the overlapping Styler rules.

Usage

Open the mod's Settings to change each setting independently. Initially, the mod keeps the active window border, removes its title bar accent color, and hides the other listed borders. Choose Windows-defined to restore Windows styling for a setting.

Under Exceptions, add an executable name such as steam.exe and select which windows to exempt under Do not hide border.

Links

  • Windows Border Switch on GitHub
  • DSN Windhawk Mods
